dedupe_keys.name: national inventory of architectural heritage niah national dataset ireland

description: The National Inventory of Architectural Heritage records Ireland's post-1700 architectural heritage on a systematic, county-by-county basis under the Architectural Heritage (National Inventory) and Historic Monuments (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1999, and its survey is the basis for the Minister's recommendations to local authorities on adding structures to their Records of Protected Structures. Each record in the open service gives a registration number, name and address with townland and county in English and Irish, original and current building type, date range, a rating, a description and appraisal, a survey image link and coordinates in Irish Transverse Mercator and latitude and longitude. Coverage: the whole state; the Buildings of Ireland site speaks of over 65,000 records for buildings and gardens, while the open buildings FeatureServer returned 48,327 features on 26 September 2026. Access: a CSV snapshot on data.gov.ie (version 11 October 2023), a live ArcGIS FeatureServer and the Historic Environment Viewer. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: inclusion in the inventory is not itself legal protection, which comes from each council's Record of Protected Structures; the CSV snapshot and the live service differ in date. Simulation uses are heritage building locations and ages for flood, storm and fire exposure and for adaptation planning. Related records: listed building registers for England and Northern Ireland, and the SEAI energy rating tool. A separate National Thatch Census (November 2022 to May 2023, CC BY 4.0) covers thatched buildings.
